NDT training in Norfolk: how it works for Norfolk employers and technicians

Short answer: NDT training for Norfolk and the Southside of Hampton Roads is delivered live online or onsite at your own shop, pier-side facility or plant. Atlantis NDT has no classroom in Norfolk. An ASNT NDT Level III teaches Level I, II and III courses in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET based on ASNT SNT-TC-1A and supports employer examinations and certification. Cohort and onsite quotes come back within one business day.

Where Newport News across the water is a shipbuilding town, Norfolk is a ship repair town. Naval Station Norfolk, the largest naval station in the world, homeports a large share of the Atlantic Fleet, and keeping those ships at sea sustains a dense cluster of private ship repair yards, pier-side contractors, machine shops and specialty subcontractors along the Elizabeth River, plus the public shipyard in Portsmouth. Repair work is faster, more varied and more schedule-driven than new construction: a technician may do UT thickness on a hull plate in the morning, MT on a foundation weld after lunch and PT on a valve body before the shift ends.

That variety is exactly why training matters here. Repair contractors need technicians certified in several methods, with records that satisfy Navy, classification society and commercial customers who each audit differently. Under SNT-TC-1A, those technicians are certified by their employer against a written practice. We help Norfolk employers build and run that system, and help individuals build the foundation that gets them hired.

Request a Norfolk training quote with your methods, levels, head-count and the specifications your customers impose.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses available in Norfolk

Each course follows the SNT-TC-1A body of knowledge for its method. For Norfolk cohorts, practical exercises lean on repair realities: corroded and pitted plate, welds made in position and in confined spaces, mixed materials in shipboard systems, and port and bridge structural steel.

MethodLevelsWhat Norfolk employers use it forPrerequisite
UTI, II, IIIHull and tank thickness gauging during availabilities; weld examination on inserts and structural repairs; bridge and port crane weldsLevel I: written-practice entry rules. Level II: Level I plus documented experience
PAUTII, IIICorrosion mapping of hull and tank plating; encoded weld examination on heavy structure and offshore wind components where specifications allowConventional UT Level II first
TOFDII, IIIThick-section weld examination and flaw sizing on heavy fabrications and foundationsUT Level II
RTI, II, IIIPiping and pressure-boundary weld repairs, valve and casting examinationVirginia radiation-safety requirements for anyone handling sources
MTI, IIFoundation, structural and fatigue-sensitive hull welds; cargo gear, crane and lifting equipment; rail and port equipmentWritten-practice entry rules
PTI, IICopper-nickel, stainless and aluminium systems, valve bodies, machined components, repair welds where MT cannot be usedWritten-practice entry rules
VTI, IIWeld and fit-up inspection on every repair, corrosion and coating condition surveys, boltingWritten-practice entry rules
ETI, II, IIIHeat-exchanger and condenser tubing on ships and in plants; crack detection through paint on structural detailsNone; prior UT or MT experience helps

UT for thickness and repair welds. Thickness gauging is the bread-and-butter UT job in ship repair: mapping hull, tank and bulkhead plating to decide what gets cropped and renewed. Our UT courses cover dual-element transducers, echo-to-echo measurement through coatings, dealing with pitted back walls and documenting readings on grids that a ship's surveyor can follow. Level II adds angle-beam examination of insert and butt welds. Test yourself with our UT Level 2 practice questions.

MT and PT. These methods account for much of the inspection volume in repair yards. Courses cover yoke and prod technique in cramped spaces, field direction, wet fluorescent versus visible particles, surface preparation on painted and corroded steel, and penetrant process control on the non-magnetic alloys common in shipboard piping and seawater systems.

VT. Visual testing is the first inspection on almost every repair. Training covers weld profile gauging, undercut and porosity assessment, lighting and access, and clear description in reports.

RT. Radiography remains common for piping and pressure repairs. The course covers exposure technique, image quality indicators, film and digital radiography and interpretation. On busy piers and inside ships, radiation exclusion zones are a real scheduling constraint, which is one reason advanced UT is gaining ground.

PAUT and TOFD. For experienced UT technicians: focal laws, encoded scans, corrosion mapping, data review and flaw sizing. Norfolk's emerging offshore wind supply chain and heavy port fabrication are likely users of these skills.

ET. Covers impedance-plane interpretation, bobbin and surface probes and calibration, steered to tubing or surface work depending on the cohort.

Level III. Live online preparation for the ASNT Basic and Method examinations and procedure writing. See ASNT Level III training.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Norfolk, step by step

  1. Written practice. Your employer adopts an SNT-TC-1A-based written practice setting training, experience, examination, vision and recertification requirements. Repair contractors working for the Navy also have to satisfy the requirements flowed down in their contracts; the employer's Level III reconciles the two.
  2. Formal training for the method and level, online, onsite or blended. Use the training-requirements matrix for SNT-TC-1A recommended figures.
  3. Supervised experience, logged and signed by a certified Level II or III. Busy repair yards can offer broad, varied experience quickly.
  4. General examination on principles, equipment and terminology.
  5. Specific examination on the employer's procedures and the acceptance criteria its customers require.
  6. Practical examination on real specimens, graded by a Level III or qualified examiner.
  7. Vision examination: near-vision acuity at least annually and colour contrast per the written practice.
  8. Certification signed by the employer.
  9. Recertification at the written-practice interval (SNT-TC-1A recommends no more than five years).

More detail: SNT-TC-1A training and certification.

Online, live-virtual or onsite NDT training for Norfolk crews

  • Live online. Instructor-led theory for Level I and II and Level III preparation, in real time and scheduled around shifts. See online NDT training.
  • Onsite at your facility. An ASNT Level III-led team teaches and examines at your shop or yard on your own equipment and representative specimens. See corporate NDT training.
  • Blended. Online theory, then a concentrated onsite practical and examination block.

Ship repair runs on availabilities, and availabilities run on the Navy's schedule. A contractor that wins work for a ship coming into a yard needs certified people on the day the ship arrives, and cannot release them mid-availability. The practical approach is to train and examine in the gaps between availabilities, or to certify new hires in batches before a large contract starts. Tell us your upcoming availability and contract dates and we will plan around them. Ask about onsite training for your Norfolk crew.

Practical examinations are always hands-on, on real equipment and specimens.

Where NDT technicians work in Norfolk

Navy ship repair. Private yards and contractors along the Elizabeth River, including BAE Systems Norfolk Ship Repair, Marine Hydraulics International, Colonna's Shipyard and General Dynamics NASSCO-Norfolk, perform maintenance and modernisation on Navy surface ships. Navy repair contractors are typically qualified under NAVSEA's Master Ship Repair Agreement or Agreement for Boat Repair, and their inspection work references NAVSEA technical publications such as T9074-AS-GIB-010/271 for NDT and MIL-STD-2035 for acceptance criteria. We name these as context for what Norfolk employers ask about. Our training is SNT-TC-1A-based; meeting NAVSEA personnel requirements is the job of the employer's programme and its Level III.

The public shipyard. Norfolk Naval Shipyard in Portsmouth, one of the Navy's four public shipyards, maintains and modernises nuclear-powered ships and qualifies its workforce through its own internal programmes. Outside training does not qualify anyone to work there, but it builds useful fundamentals.

Commercial marine and the port. The Port of Virginia's terminals, including Norfolk International Terminals and the coal piers at Lamberts Point, bring crane, conveyor and structural inspection. Commercial vessel repair follows ABS or other classification society rules and U.S. Coast Guard requirements.

Offshore wind. Dominion Energy's Coastal Virginia Offshore Wind project uses Portsmouth Marine Terminal as a staging and marshalling base. Offshore wind structures involve heavy welded steel inspected with UT, PAUT, MT and VT, often to DNV or client specifications.

Bridges and tunnels. The Hampton Roads Bridge-Tunnel expansion, the Chesapeake Bay Bridge-Tunnel and the region's many moveable and fixed bridges need structural steel inspection, typically to AWS D1.5 for bridge welding and VDOT specifications.

Aviation and industry. Naval air stations in the region support aircraft maintenance, which usually follows NAS 410 or military requirements, a separate scheme. Manufacturing, rail equipment and industrial plants around Chesapeake and Suffolk commonly certify under SNT-TC-1A.

Radiography licensing in Virginia. Virginia has been an NRC Agreement State since March 31, 2009. The Virginia Department of Health's Office of Radiological Health licenses radioactive materials, including industrial radiography sources, under the Virginia Radiation Protection Regulations (12VAC5-481). Radiographer training and certification must meet those regulations and the company's licence conditions, and out-of-state firms use Virginia's reciprocity process. This is separate from SNT-TC-1A RT certification: a Norfolk radiographer usually needs both.

What employers ask for. Current method certifications and the written practice behind them, complete training and experience records, a current vision record, a TWIC card for port and many shipyard facilities, and base access credentials for work on Navy installations. For pay information we point to public sources in our NDT salary guide.

Level III services and written practices for Norfolk NDT companies

Hampton Roads has many small repair subcontractors, and many of them lean on one or two senior technicians rather than a dedicated Level III. That works until a prime contractor or Navy auditor asks for the written practice, examination records and procedures. We help with:

  • Written practice development and review matched to the methods you use and the requirements your customers flow down. See written practice development.
  • Examination preparation and grading under ASNT Level III oversight, with records filed for audit.
  • Procedure writing with Level III review of technique and reporting formats.
  • Audit preparation: a structured pass through certification files before a customer visit.

See the SNT-TC-1A guidance page for background. Book a Level III consultation before your next audit or availability.

Practise before the practical exam

The Practical NDT 3D simulator offers 12 NDT methods in 5 environments: an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. Norfolk repair trainees get most from the welding workshop and storage tank scenes, which are closest to plate, weld and thickness work. It helps trainees rehearse setups, coverage and interpretation between classes. It is practice only: it does not replace hands-on training, logged experience or the practical examination on real specimens.

Your instructor

Training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT, who sets course content, oversees examinations and reviews written practices and procedures for employer clients.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Norfolk

How do I get NDT certified in Norfolk?

Work for or be sponsored by an employer with an SNT-TC-1A written practice, complete training, log supervised experience, pass the general, specific and practical examinations and a vision test, and the employer certifies you. We provide training, exam preparation and Level III support online or onsite.

Can I take NDT training online in Virginia?

Yes, for the theory portion. Practical training and practical examinations are hands-on.

Which methods do Norfolk ship repair contractors need most?

VT, MT and UT thickness, followed by PT and RT. Technicians certified in several methods are the most useful to repair employers.

How long does UT Level 2 training take?

It is set by your employer's written practice, based on SNT-TC-1A recommended training and experience hours. Experience is usually the longer part. See the training-requirements matrix.

Do I need a license for radiography in Virginia?

Yes: the company needs a Virginia radioactive materials licence or machine registration, and radiographers must meet the state's training and certification requirements. That is separate from SNT-TC-1A RT certification.

What does NDT training cost in Norfolk?

We do not publish prices. Cost depends on method, level, group size, delivery mode and any Level III support. Send your details and we quote within one business day.

Is ASNT certification recognised by Norfolk employers?

SNT-TC-1A-based programmes are common among repair, port, bridge and industrial employers. Navy contracts add NAVSEA requirements met through the employer's programme, and aviation employers may require NAS 410. Recognition runs through the employer's written practice.

Will your training get me into Norfolk Naval Shipyard?

No outside course qualifies you to work at the public shipyard, which trains its own workforce. Solid SNT-TC-1A fundamentals are good preparation for any marine NDT role.

Can you help with offshore wind inspection skills?

We teach UT, PAUT, TOFD, MT and VT under SNT-TC-1A. Offshore wind clients may also impose their own specifications or other schemes; we tell you plainly which parts we cover.

Can you certify our crew between availabilities?

Yes. We plan onsite training and examinations under your written practice to fit the gaps in your schedule.

Does my certification transfer to another contractor?

Not automatically. The new employer reviews your records and certifies you under its own written practice.

Do you offer Level III preparation?

Yes, live online. See Level III training and our full training catalogue.
